data.general#General: Is GradLab free to use?Yes. GradLab is free and runs entirely in your browser with no account required.Do I need to install anything?No. GradLab runs as a web application — open the URL and start creating. No plugins, no desktop app, no dependencies.Which browsers are supported?Any browser with WebGL support: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge on desktop and mobile. For video recording, Chrome and Edge offer the best codec support (MP4/H.264). Safari exports WebM as fallback.Is my work saved automatically?GradLab is session-based — your settings persist while the page is open. To preserve a configuration, use Export Code to save a self-contained HTML file with all parameters embedded.
data.export--quality#Export & Quality: What resolution are exported PNGs?PNG exports match the WebGL render buffer, which renders at Math.max(2, devicePixelRatio). On a standard display, a maximized browser window produces an export roughly twice the screen resolution. On Retina/HiDPI displays, resolution is higher still.Can I export a transparent PNG?Not currently. The canvas renders against a solid background. Transparency can be added in any image editor using the corner-radius alpha channel as a starting mask.My video export is WebM, not MP4 — why?MP4 (H.264) encoding requires MediaRecorder H.264 support, which varies by browser. Safari and some Firefox configurations fall back to WebM (VP8). Both are widely compatible; WebM plays natively in all modern browsers.
data.performance#Performance: The animation is stuttering — what should I do?Try reducing the Speed slider and disabling the ASCII Matrix layer if enabled — the character grid is CPU-intensive at large sizes. Closing other GPU-heavy browser tabs can also help.Does GradLab work on mobile?Yes. The WebGL engine runs on mobile browsers. Note that video recording is not available on iOS due to MediaRecorder API limitations. PNG export and HTML export work on all platforms.
data.use-cases#Use Cases: Can I use GradLab outputs in commercial projects?Yes. Exports are yours to use. There are no watermarks or usage restrictions on exported PNG, video, or HTML files.How do I embed the gradient in my website?Use Export Code to get a self-contained HTML file, then embed it via <iframe> in your page. Set width: 100% and height: 100% on the iframe for a full-bleed background.Can I use the exported gradient as a video background?Yes. Export a short MP4 or WebM clip with Ping-pong Loop enabled, then use it as an HTML5 <video> with autoplay loop muted playsinline. This is the most performant approach for animated backgrounds in production websites.

data: The ASCII Matrix renders a full-canvas grid of characters over the gradient layer. Characters respond to mouse proximity in real time — brightening, shifting, or decaying based on where the cursor moves — creating a dynamic, interactive typographic texture.The matrix runs on a separate canvas layer composited over the WebGL output, keeping it visually controllable without affecting the underlying gradient animation.

Classic ASCII brightness mapping	Blocks	██▓▒░ 	Chunky, graphic block shading	Detailed	Full 70-character luminance ramp	Maximum tonal detail	Minimal	·■ 	Ultra-sparse, geometric	Binary	01	Data / cyberpunk feel	Custom	Your text	Brand name, keyword, any string
data.custom-charset#Custom Charset: Enter any text in the custom field — a brand name, a phrase, a single repeated character — and the matrix tiles it across the canvas. Combined with a large font size, this is an effective way to embed text as texture.
data.mouse-interaction#Mouse Interaction:
Move the cursor over the canvas to activate the heatmap. Characters within the Interaction Radius respond with increased brightness and animation activity.
Parameter	Effect	Radius	Size of the interaction zone around the cursor	Decay	How quickly characters return to their resting state after the cursor leaves	Smooth	Easing on the interaction response — higher values produce a softer, more gradual activation	Gravity	Pulls activated characters toward the cursor; at 0 characters stay in place
data.display-controls#Display Controls: Parameter	Effect	Size	Font size of each character cell	Spacing	Line-height multiplier — tighter values pack characters closer vertically	Font	Selects from a set of monospaced typefaces	Color	The fill color of the characters	Blend Mode	How the character layer composites over the gradient
data.blend-modes#Blend Modes: Blend Mode	Effect	Overlay	Characters take on the gradient's hue — natural integration	Screen	Characters always lighten — works well on dark gradients	Multiply	Characters always darken — works well on light gradients	Normal	Flat character color over the gradient, no blending
data.interaction-mode#Interaction Mode:
Mode	Description	Heatmap Decay	Characters brighten on cursor contact, then fade back — decay leaves a glowing trail	Dynamic Background	The full character grid animates continuously; cursor interaction shifts character density	
For landing page hero sections, try Code charset at a medium size with Overlay blend and a 20% decay — it creates a living background texture that doesn't compete with foreground text.

data: GradLab offers three export formats. All exports capture the full composited output — gradient, halftone, ASCII matrix, and grain — at the native render resolution (minimum 2× device pixel ratio).
data.png-screenshot#PNG Screenshot:
Download Frame captures the current canvas state as a PNG.
Resolution matches the WebGL render buffer — minimum 2× device pixel ratio
Includes all active layers: gradient, halftone, ASCII matrix, and film grain
Corner radius is embedded in the PNG alpha channel if enabled
Instant — no processing delay
When to use: static assets for presentations, social media, UI mockups, or print.
data.video-recording#Video Recording:
Record MP4 captures a live video of the animation.
Click Record MP4 to begin — the button shows an elapsed timer
Click Stop when done
GradLab encodes the captured frames and downloads the file
Setting	Options	Format	MP4 (H.264) when supported; WebM (VP8) as fallback	Ping-pong Loop	When enabled, the recording plays forward then reverses for a seamless infinite loop	
Enable Ping-pong Loop before starting the recording if you intend to use the video as a looping background. The resulting file loops without a visible cut point.
Tips for clean recordings:
Record a short clip (3–8 seconds) and rely on ping-pong loop for looping — keeps file sizes small
Lower Speed before recording for a slower, more atmospheric loop
Disable 3D Tilt — it is screen-relative and produces inconsistent motion in the exported file
data.html-code-export#HTML Code Export:
Export Code produces a fully self-contained .html file containing:
The complete WebGL shader source
All current parameter values embedded as uniforms
The canvas rendering loop
No external dependencies — the file runs in any browser offline
The resulting HTML can be:
Dropped into an <iframe> in any web project
Used as a standalone full-screen background
Opened directly as a file in any browser
Shared as a single-file artifact with all visual state preserved
The exported HTML is a snapshot of your current settings. If you adjust the gradient after exporting, export again — there is no live link between the HTML file and the app.
data.resolution-notes#Resolution Notes:
GradLab renders at Math.max(2, devicePixelRatio), guaranteeing consistent output across all platforms:
Mac (Retina): 2× or 3× depending on display
Windows (standard DPI): renders at 2× regardless of OS DPI setting

data: The Halftone layer converts the continuous gradient into a pattern of discrete dots or shapes, mimicking traditional print halftone screens. It's rendered as a GPU compositing pass over the base gradient, giving you full control over density, shape, and contrast without affecting the underlying animation.
data.dither-matrix#Dither Matrix: Matrix	Character	Random	Stochastic noise — irregular, organic dot placement with no visible grid	2×2 Ordered	A 2-cell Bayer matrix — visible grid structure, retro digital feel	4×4 Ordered	A 16-step Bayer matrix — smoother tonal range with a classic halftone grid	8×8 Ordered	High-precision Bayer matrix — fine dot control, closest to commercial print halftone
data.dot-shape#Dot Shape: Shape	Description	Circle	Classic halftone dot — the most common print and editorial look	Square	Hard-edged blocks — bold, graphic, pixel-art adjacent	Diamond	45° rotated square — produces a distinctive angular grid	Line	Parallel stripes — resembles mezzotint or engraving screens	Cross	Star-shaped dots — decorative, maximalist texture	Ellipse	Horizontally stretched dots — softer than circle, more directional
data.size#Size: Controls the diameter of each dot cell. Smaller values produce fine, high-frequency halftone screens; larger values produce bold, chunky dots that read clearly at a distance.
data.contrast#Contrast:
Shifts the luminance threshold at which dots appear. Increase contrast to push dots toward full-on or full-off; decrease to preserve gradient tonal nuance within the pattern.
Combine 8×8 Ordered dither with Circle shape and a low contrast setting to get the closest result to traditional offset print halftone. Pair with a two-color palette for a spot-color print aesthetic.
data.use-cases#Use Cases:
Editorial design — halftone backgrounds for magazine-style layouts
Risograph / screen print — simulate ink-on-paper printing aesthetics
Brand visuals — add texture and depth to gradient backgrounds
Retro UI — combine with a limited palette for a nostalgic digital feel

data: The Palette panel is the foundation of every gradient. GradLab blends your chosen colors across the canvas using the OKLab perceptual color space, which preserves luminance balance and saturation at every point — avoiding the muddy midtones common in standard RGB blending.
data.adding-and-removing-colors#Adding and Re:
Click + to add a new color (maximum 8)
Click the × on any swatch to remove it (minimum 2)
Colors render in the order they appear in the panel
data.reordering#Reordering: Drag any color swatch left or right to change its position in the blend sequence. The canvas updates in real time as you drag.
data.color-picker#Color Picker:
Click a swatch to open the color picker. You can:
Interact with the hue/saturation/lightness gradient field
Type a hex code directly into the input field
The picker remembers the previous color if you cancel
data.blend-mode#Blend Mode:
The Blend Mode toggle switches between two color interpolation methods:
Mode	Description	OKLab	Perceptually uniform — smooth, vivid blends across all hue pairs	RGB	Standard linear interpolation — may produce dull midtones on complementary pairs	
OKLab is the default and recommended setting for most use cases.
data.blend-bias--sharpness#Blend Bias & Sharp:
Blend Bias shifts the interpolation midpoint — push toward 0 to weight the gradient toward your first color, toward 100 to weight toward the last
Blend Sharpness controls how abruptly colors transition; higher values produce more distinct color bands rather than smooth fades
data.image-color-extraction#Image Color Extra:
Click the image icon next to the color list to upload a photo. GradLab samples the dominant colors from the image and populates the palette automatically.
Try uploading a sunset photo or a design reference — the extracted palette often produces gradient starting points that would take minutes to build manually.

data: Post-processing effects are applied on top of the rendered gradient as a compositing pass. They are non-destructive — adjusting or disabling them never changes the underlying shader output.
data.film-grain#Film Grain:
Film grain adds a layer of analog noise over the canvas, simulating the texture of photographic film or printed media.
Intensity — controls how visible the grain is, from imperceptible texture to heavy noise
Blend Mode — determines how the grain interacts with the gradient beneath it
Blend Mode	Effect	Overlay	Grain lightens highlights and darkens shadows — the most natural film look	Screen	Grain only brightens, adding a luminous haze	Multiply	Grain only darkens, adding depth and grit	
Grain at 15–25 intensity with Overlay blend gives the gradient a subtle tactile quality that prints especially well.
data.inner-border#Inner Border:
Adds a soft vignette or hard frame inside the canvas edges.
Increases visual depth and focus on the center
Works well for social media formats where you want the gradient contained rather than bleeding to the edges
Adjustable radius controls how far the border extends inward
data.corner-radius#Corner Radius:
Rounds the corners of the rendered canvas. The exported PNG and HTML both respect the corner radius, producing output that can be dropped directly into rounded-corner UI components without masking.
0 — perfectly square corners
Higher values — progressively rounded, up to a full circle at maximum
data.3d-tilt#3D Tilt:
Adds a subtle perspective warp to the canvas that responds to mouse movement. As the cursor moves across the page, the gradient tilts along the X and Y axes, creating a parallax depth illusion.
Zero cost to the WebGL render pass
Disabled automatically during video recording to keep exported loops clean
3D Tilt is a preview-only effect and does not affect PNG or video exports.

data: Shape & Flow defines the underlying mathematical structure that drives your gradient's motion and form. Each algorithm runs entirely on the GPU as a GLSL fragment shader, enabling smooth 60fps animation even on complex patterns.
data.classic--periodic#Classic & Periodic: Algorithm	Character	Sin/Cos (Classic)	Smooth, wave-based periodic gradients. The most predictable starting point — great for calm, flowing aesthetics.	Structured Mapping (Order)	Organized, grid-like spatial mapping. Produces ordered, geometric gradient structures.	Linear Stratified (Vertical)	Horizontal layered bands with subtle variation — clean, architectural.
data.organic--chaotic#Organic & Chaotic: Algorithm	Character	Fluid Dynamics (Chaos)	Simulates turbulent fluid motion using layered noise. High entropy, organic, unpredictable.	Domain Warp (Marble)	Iteratively warps UV coordinates to produce marble-like veining and folded structures.	Curl Noise (Vortex)	Derives motion from the curl of a noise field — smooth, divergence-free swirling vortices.	Polar Vortex (Cosmic)	Combines polar coordinates with noise for cosmic spiral structures.
data.topology--geometry#Topology & Geometry: Algorithm	Character	Radial Topography (Rings)	Concentric rings radiating from the canvas center, reminiscent of contour maps or sound wave visualizations.	Conic Sweep (Angular)	Angular color sweeps derived from polar angles — pie-chart-like sectors with smooth gradient transitions.	Nested SDF Shape (Core Glow)	Uses signed-distance field math to render a geometric shape with a glowing core. Clean, sharp, sculptural.
data.diffusion#Diffusion:
Diffusion algorithms push gradient colors through a simulated diffusion field, producing soft, organic spread with optional texture sourcing.
Algorithm	Character	Diffusion Gradient (Organic)	Pure procedural diffusion — soft, natural color spread without hard edges.	Diffusion Fluid (Image)	Upload a background image; the diffusion field warps and blends it into the gradient.	Diffusion Fluid (Procedural SDF)	Uses multi-point signed-distance fields as the diffusion source — geometric but organic.
data.motion-controls#Motion Controls: Parameter	Effect	Speed	How fast the animation progresses. 0 freezes the frame; higher values produce rapid motion.	Zoom	Spatial scale of the pattern — zoom in for close-up detail, zoom out for a broad view.	Liquid	Blends between the algorithm's structured output and a fluid noise layer.	Morph	Context-sensitive. On wave-based algorithms it adjusts wave distortion; on SDF shapes it morphs the base geometry.
data.camera-pan#Camera Pan:
Click and drag directly on the canvas to pan the view. Works on all algorithms and lets you frame the exact portion of the pattern you want.
Pan position is stored per-preset, so switching presets restores the last-used camera position for that preset.

data: GradLab is a browser-based creative tool for generating high-quality gradient visuals. It combines a GPU-accelerated WebGL shader engine with a precision color pipeline built on the OKLab perceptual color space, ensuring every blend looks natural regardless of hue.Whether you're crafting a visual identity background, a motion loop for social media, or an interactive art piece, GradLab gives you professional-grade controls without any installation.
data.why-gradlab#Why GradLab:
Most gradient tools work in sRGB space, which causes muddy or overly dark blends when mixing complementary colors. GradLab routes every color operation through OKLab — a perceptually uniform color space — so transitions remain vivid and balanced at every step.The rendering pipeline runs on your GPU via WebGL, meaning:
No server round-trips. Every parameter change is rendered locally, instantly.
No installation. Open the URL and start creating.
High resolution output. Renders at 2× device pixel ratio minimum for crisp exports on all platforms.

data: GradLab requires WebGL support. Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge all support WebGL by default on desktop and mobile.
data.open-gradlab#Open GradLab: Navigate to gradlab.app in any modern browser. The canvas begins rendering immediately using one of three built-in presets. No sign-up required.
data.choose-a-preset#Choose a Preset: Three presets appear at the top of the control panel. Click any to load a full configuration — colors, flow algorithm, and post-processing included.Use presets as a starting point, not a final result. Every parameter is editable after loading.
data.set-your-colors#Set Your Colors:
In the Palette section, click any color swatch to open the color picker. You can:
Type a hex code directly
Drag swatches to reorder the blend sequence
Click the image icon to extract colors from a photo
Add up to 8 colors, remove down to 2
Colors are blended in OKLab space by default, producing smooth, perceptually uniform transitions.
data.pick-a-flow-algorithm#Pick a Flow Algori:
Open Shape & Flow and choose one of 13 algorithms from the dropdown. Each algorithm defines the underlying motion structure of the gradient:
Sin/Cos (Classic) — smooth periodic waves, a reliable starting point
Fluid Dynamics (Chaos) — turbulent, organic motion
Radial Topography (Rings) — concentric rings radiating from center
Nested SDF Shape (Core Glow) — geometric glow emanating from a signed-distance field shape
Use the Speed, Zoom, Liquid, and Morph sliders to fine-tune the motion feel.
data.adjust-post-processing-optional#Adjust P:
In the Post-Processing panel you can add:
Film Grain — analog texture over the gradient
Inner Border — a soft or hard vignette frame
3D Tilt — a subtle perspective warp that responds to mouse movement
data.export#Export:
When the canvas looks right, choose your export format:
Button	Output	Download Frame	PNG screenshot at full resolution	Record MP4	Click to start, click to stop — exports MP4 or WebM	Export Code	Self-contained HTML file you can embed anywhere	
Enable Ping-pong Loop before recording to get a seamlessly looping video — perfect for social media or UI backgrounds.
